transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Katherine Lewis (Ridgewater Head of Security), Marcus Brown (Cloud Architect), Sofia Perez (PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on security/compliance items during the pilot: SSO (SAML), audit log formats and retention, SOC 2 scope, KMS options for encryption, and data residency notes. Agreed next steps for sharing docs and a small audit-log ingest example to validate our SIEM pipeline.

Topics:
- SAML SSO & IdP attributes
- Audit logs: format, retention, and export
- SOC 2 evidence and scope for the POC
- Encryption/KMS and key custody options
- Data retention, deletion API, and legal hold

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Katherine, Marcus, Sofia, Omar and myself. Good to see you all.
[00:18] Katherine Lewis: hi yes thanks, we're doing well. we'll jump in, our security lead asked for a couple of specifics this week around audit logs and the SSO flow.
[00:27] Marcus Brown: and we've got some live traffic patterns to share. want to validate that your export can land into our Splunk - or we might use S3 + lambda to forward.
[00:40] Omar Patel: yeah, we can do both. i can attach a sample payload, there's a couple of variations depending on whether it's hosted vs dedicated. note, the field names might be slightly different, auto transcriber sometimes makes those look weird.
[00:55] Sofia Perez: quick question — is the SOC2 report you mentioned in the last call scoped to multi-tenant hosted only or does it include Dedicated/Private?
[01:05] Maya Chen: good question. the SOC2 Type II we provide covers Redwood's hosted control plane and infra — the report explicitly calls out our production hosted offering. for Dedicated we have an addendum and for Private deployments we provide implementation guidance; we can surface the relevant controls and gaps for your security team.
[01:22] Katherine Lewis: ok we need that scope spelled out. also we have to confirm encryption at rest and key management - we use a customer-managed KMS in AWS for anything with PII. can Redwood support a bring-your-own-key pattern?
[01:34] Omar Patel: yes, for the Private deployment we support CMK via KMS/HSM, and for Dedicated we have a KMS integration pattern that can be customer-managed — with caveats on root key rotation windows. for hosted, we use our managed keys but we do have envelope encryption and can support customer-managed keys for enterprise customers under contract.
[01:50] Marcus Brown: what about audit logs and the granularity? we need user-level tracing, token-level cost info, and the actual request payload hashes for provenance.
[02:02] Omar Patel: our audit logs contain event types like request.create, auth.login, model.invoke, and admin.change. each event includes timestamp, user_id (or SSO subject), route, model_id, and a redacted payload reference — we don't put full PII in the logs by default. we can toggle more verbose logging inside a Dedicated or Private pilot.
[02:28] Katherine Lewis: can you produce a sample that matches Splunk's JSON ingest? sometimes the names get renamed — like 'model.invoke' shows as 'model_call' in other systems.
[02:37] Omar Patel: totally. i'll export a sample and include a mapping table. note — sometimes the SDK emits slightly different field names depending on SDK version; i'll include both v2 and v3 examples.
[02:49] Maya Chen: also, on retention — what's your default retention for logs in hosted? we need to compare to our policy: 7 years for certain transaction traces, but operationally we might only keep 90 days hot.
[03:03] Omar Patel: hosted default is 90 days for high-fidelity logs, with 1 year for aggregated billing/usage metrics. we can provide long-term exports to your S3 for your archival needs; that's what most banks do to meet long retention. for Private/Dedicated you control retention.
[03:18] Marcus Brown: good. what about deletion APIs — we have to be able to purge PII on request and demonstrate deletion. is there an admin deletion endpoint?
[03:26] Omar Patel: yes, there's a deletion API and built-in data lifecycle policies. however, for hosted there are operational steps we need to coordinate for full deep deletion if data is cached in KV caches; we document TTLs and how to validate deletion. for Dedicated/Private it's straightforward because you control storage.
[03:43] Katherine Lewis: SOC2 evidence — can you provide evidence for access controls, change management, and logging? we'll need the controls mapped to our questionnaire.
[03:52] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll send the SOC2 Type II and a control mapping spreadsheet that ties our controls to common questionnaires. and we'll flag which controls are customer responsibilities in Dedicated/Private setups.
[04:05] Sofia Perez: one item from product — during the POC we hit a scenario where the SSO session timed out early; is that something configurable on your end or IdP?
[04:14] Omar Patel: session lifetime is negotiable — default is 1 hour for the web console but tokens for API are longer based on refresh. often that's controlled by IdP. we can support SAML assertions with session indexes and enforce session SLOs on our side too.
[04:30] Marcus Brown: on SAML attributes — we need group membership and role mappings. can you accept custom attributes like dept and role_level?
[04:39] Omar Patel: yes. we map SAML attributes to RBAC entries. i'll include sample metadata and a mapping doc. we have a policy for handling missing attributes — fallback to a default role.
[04:52] Katherine Lewis: any compliance concerns around data residency? some of our customers require EU-only processing.
[04:58] Maya Chen: we have region tagging and can pin workloads to EU regions for hosted, and of course Dedicated/Private can be deployed inside your VPC or an on-prem instance for full residency. we'll surface the latency/cost tradeoffs if you want EU-only serving.
[05:12] Sofia Perez: re: benching — we wanted to run a 10k token sample to see memory/kv cache behavior. is that something we can run in the POC environment?
[05:21] Omar Patel: yes, we can spin a dedicated test harness; if you want low-level metrics we'll give GPU util, per-token latency histograms, and kv cache miss rates. for Hosted sometimes we route to a compatible model variant, so to get deterministic results Dedicated is preferred.
[05:41] Marcus Brown: ok noted. any blockers on our side for SSO setup?
[05:45] Maya Chen: we just need your IdP metadata XML and a list of SAML attributes to map. Marcus?
[05:52] Marcus Brown: i'll pull that from our dev idp and share.
[05:55] Katherine Lewis: two risk items: 1) audit-log tamper proofing — do you support signed logs or append-only storage? 2) evidence retention for e-discovery.
[06:06] Omar Patel: for tamper proofing we can ship logs to your S3 with server-side encryption and object lock for append-only. for hosted we can also stream to an external SIEM (Splunk) to maintain an immutable copy. evidence retention/e-discovery — we'll coordinate exports and snapshots; we have export tooling for the POC.
[06:26] Sofia Perez: can you demonstrate the log-forwarding in the next call?
[06:30] Maya Chen: yes — next steps we'll have Omar send samples and then do a short demo of ingest.
[06:36] Katherine Lewis: about data masking — when models process PII, do you do automated redaction in outputs or is that developer responsibility?
[06:45] Omar Patel: we offer optional pre-processing hooks and a redaction library, but we recommend customers do application-level PII redaction for sensitive workloads. we can show patterns for both.
[06:58] Marcus Brown: one more — in case of an incident will Redwood provide audit trails and timelines for the forensic packet?
[07:06] Maya Chen: yes, incident response includes audit trails and a post-mortem package for enterprise customers; the SLA includes timeline commitments for initial contact and forensic artifacts availability.
[07:18] Katherine Lewis: great. on legal hold — sometimes legal asks to freeze deletion for an investigation. can you disable retention policies on demand?
[07:26] Omar Patel: for Dedicated/Private yes. for hosted we have an operational procedure to suspend deletion and snapshot relevant datasets — but we do require formal requests and legal contact emails. we'll include the runbook.
[07:40] Sofia Perez: timeline check — SOC2 docs by Friday, SAML metadata by next Tuesday, sample logs ASAP?
[07:48] Maya Chen: yep. i'll send SOC2 and compliance pack by Friday EOD. Omar will drop logs and mapping today or tomorrow. Marcus to confirm IdP metadata by Tuesday.
[07:58] Katherine Lewis: sounds good. one last item: vulnerability scanning frequency and pen test reports?
[08:05] Omar Patel: we perform quarterly scans and an annual external pen test; we'll surface the most recent summary and remediation timeline.
[08:15] Maya Chen: ok, recap of action items and next steps coming in the calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[08:20] Katherine Lewis: thanks all.
[08:22] End of meeting.
